authorization: plan and mock source authoring boundaries only, pending root reservation; no real provider or runtime

sections.Decision: PLAN_GO for author reservation of the four listed, unconnected files only. Rules receive plain synthetic inputs. The adapter requires an injected transport and trusted fixed project configuration. Mocks are in-memory. Keep imports side-effect free, with no default fetch, environment reads, SDK initialization, registry edits, routes, UI, schema, package edits or application wiring. No test or provider request ran in this review.
sections.Rules and caller boundary: Use project email normalization semantics, preserve plus/dot distinctions, and treat same canonical address as unchanged. Take the privileged-address exclusions as explicit trusted input and deny both privileged current and target addresses. Pending/current address, account UUID, version and chosen old/new mailbox come from trusted caller state. Never accept an actor, pending target or proof destination from form authority. Unexpired identical pending requests must not automatically resend. Keep cancellation/expiry/restart policy outside the mocks until product policy is recorded.
sections.Fresh password and actor binding: Mock only the fixed password grant and, where needed, GET /auth/v1/user. Bind the actual access bearer used for PUT to the expected immutable account UUID, confirmed current email and an owned provider=email identity matching that address. Distinguish the identity row ID from identity.user_id; never substitute display/user metadata or a decoded but unverified token. Use the actual bearer on /user before PUT when the grant representation cannot prove the binding; an unconditional authenticated /user check is also a small closed implementation. Reject mismatches, empty tokens, malformed success, anonymous/SSO/unsupported accounts, verified MFA or unclear factor evidence. A provider-documented factors omission in a trusted complete representation must be distinguished from missing evidence in a partial body. Password failure or provider uncertainty cannot fall back to local crypt, MFA bypass, signup/invite/reset helpers or service/admin credentials. The published model and gateway identify these provider fields and AAL behavior. [Identity model](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/ae468cabab7359819730ca80b5c6178def3579a2/internal/models/identity.go#L12-L25) · [User model](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/ae468cabab7359819730ca80b5c6178def3579a2/internal/models/user.go#L53-L62) · [User update](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/ae468cabab7359819730ca80b5c6178def3579a2/internal/api/user.go#L87-L122)
sections.Mutation contract: The sole begin mutation is PUT /auth/v1/user with the fresh user bearer and only the normalized email field. Reserve the request origin/path/method and JSON shape inside the adapter. No caller-selected URLs or redirects, secret-bearing URLs, metadata update, password mutation, confirmation flag or administrative endpoint. Inject a fake transport only; enforce an abortable finite deadline, redirect:error and no retries. Distinguish definite pre-send rejection from timeout/response loss after a possible write. On uncertainty return a fixed unknown outcome requiring canonical reread; sending a second request is unsafe. A successful begin means request accepted and pending, not delivery or mailbox verification. Same-server reauthorization between grant and mutation remains a future controller responsibility. [Provider update](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/ae468cabab7359819730ca80b5c6178def3579a2/internal/api/user.go)
sections.OTP and completion: Use POST /auth/v1/verify with type=email_change, a token preserved as a string and the appropriate trusted current or pending address. Model both proof orders. The pinned first-leg response is a specific 200 message/code envelope without a completed user. Classify that recognizable response as partial, never classify arbitrary empty 200, contradictory fields or malformed JSON as accepted proof. A final provider response must identify exactly the expected UUID and target canonical email with a matching owned email identity and confirmation evidence. Neither an old email_confirmed_at, an unchanged old identity, nor a returned session token proves target ownership. Emit at most a provider-final candidate requiring canonical same-user target/identity readback before application success or reconciliation. Bad/expired/replayed codes do not automatically clear, restart or resend a pending request. Never sign the application in with tokens returned by verification. [Provider verify](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/ae468cabab7359819730ca80b5c6178def3579a2/internal/api/verify.go#L225-L292)
sections.Mock acceptance: Before mock execution independently review the four exact files. Minimum negatives cover spoofed grant user/bearer, foreign identity owner, wrong target, missing/unconfirmed email identity, verified provider factor, unsafe redirect, malformed responses, OTP retaining a leading zero, ambiguous timeout before/after a mutation, and no automatic second request. Positives cover genuine password grant + bound identity, exact one PUT, both orders of dual proof and final candidate pending trusted reread. Assert exact routes/header roles/body using synthetic sentinels without printed credentials. Public outputs and caught errors expose only fixed business states. Passwords, OTPs, bearer/refresh tokens, raw response bodies and identifying mailbox text do not enter logs, receipts, snapshots or caller-visible error messages. Return no general-purpose token capability to routes or DTOs.
sections.Outstanding approvals: Ron’s both-mailbox, expiry/start-over and leave-page/cancel decisions, PE exact deployed version, secure-change enabled, autoconfirm off, real OTP template/length/lifetime, redirect and send/rate controls remain outstanding prerequisites for runtime work. Provider commit and canonical application reconciliation are separate operations. Live authority/consent/partner gates, recovery of partial remote commits, session/reset/challenge invalidation, profile mirrors and safe old-code rollback remain for later review. No real address change, mailbox delivery, new storage, target readiness, pilot or whole B016 acceptance follows from this plan. The published canonical-email code checkpoint and open browser failure remain separate.
